transcript.text: If you still use VLOOKUP, this one's for you.
In the next minute you'll see why XLOOKUP is simply better.
Here's a price list: product codes on the left, prices on the right.
With VLOOKUP you count columns: lookup value, the whole table,
column number three, and FALSE for an exact match.
Insert a column and that three is wrong. Silently.
XLOOKUP takes three things: what you look for,
where to look, and what to return.
No column numbers, no FALSE at the end.
It looks to the left too, which VLOOKUP never could.
Not found? The fourth argument says what to show instead,
like "not in the list", instead of an ugly #N/A.
And it can return a whole row at once: price, stock and supplier.
One catch: XLOOKUP needs Excel 2021 or Microsoft 365.
On older versions, INDEX and MATCH do the same job.
Download the practice file from the link in the description
and try it on your own data.
Which lookup do you use? Tell me in the comments.
